events.title: Building the Dong Thap Muoi Resistance Base
events.description: After the French army captured Gia Dinh, Thien Ho Duong (Vo Duy Duong) and Doc Binh Kieu withdrew their troops to the Dong Thap Muoi wetlands to build an anti-French base. The insurgent army relied on the rugged terrain to organize guerrilla warfare, causing heavy losses to the enemy during the 1864-1866 period.

events.title: Pho Bang Nguyen Sinh Sac passed away in Cao Lanh
events.description: Pho Bang Nguyen Sinh Sac (father of President Ho Chi Minh), after a period of patriotic activities and practicing traditional medicine to treat the people, passed away in Hoa An Village, Cao Lanh. His tomb has become an especially important historical and cultural relic of the province.

events.title: Establishment of the first Annam Communist Party Cell
events.description: In Hoa An Village (Cao Lanh), the first Annam Communist Party Cell of the former Sa Dec Province was established with Comrade Pham Huu Lau as Secretary. This was the core leadership of the revolutionary movement in the Cao Lanh - Dong Thap Muoi region.

events.title: Seizing power in Cao Lanh and Sa Dec
events.description: Joining the spirit of the General Uprising, the masses rose up to seize power in Sa Dec provincial capital and Cao Lanh district capital. The puppet government collapsed, and the Provisional Administrative Committee was introduced to the people.

events.title: Giong Thi Dam - Go Quan Cung Victory
events.description: The newly established 502nd Battalion (the province's main force unit) organized a daring ambush, defeating a French military operation, wiping out both enemy army and navy forces, and capturing nearly 100 soldiers. This was a resounding opening victory for the armed forces of Dong Thap Muoi.

events.title: The 100-day troop regrouping event (Cao Lanh)
events.description: Cao Lanh was chosen as one of the three major troop regrouping points in the South (along with Ca Mau and Xuyen Moc) to transfer Southern cadres and soldiers to the North under the Geneva Accords. During the 100 days, the military and people of Cao Lanh welcomed and saw off tens of thousands of Southern children.

events.title: Sinking the Small Fleet on rivers and canals
events.description: The military and people of Dong Thap creatively developed naval commando tactics, using homemade water mines to sink many warships belonging to the US 'Small Fleet' on the dense network of rivers and canals, defeating the enemy's 'Mobile Riverine Force' tactic on the Mekong River.

events.title: Liberation of Dong Thap Province (Kien Phong and Sa Dec)
events.description: The provincial armed forces coordinated with the rising masses to attack Cao Lanh Town (the provincial capital of Kien Phong) and Sa Dec Town. By noon on April 30, the liberation flag flew over the Governor's Palaces of Kien Phong and Sa Dec, and the entire province was completely liberated.

events.title: Establishment of Dong Thap Province
events.description: Implementing the Government's Resolution, Kien Phong Province and Sa Dec Province were merged into Dong Thap Province. The provincial capital was initially located in Sa Dec Town, then moved to Cao Lanh Town (now Cao Lanh City) in 1994.

events.title: Go Thap Relic recognized as a Special National Relic
events.description: The Go Thap Relic Area—which contains important traces of the ancient Oc Eo culture and the history of land reclamation and resistance against foreign invaders of this land—was officially classified as a Special National Relic by the Prime Minister.

events.title: Tram Chim National Park becomes a Ramsar site
events.description: Tram Chim National Park (home to the conservation of the rare Red-crowned Crane) was recognized as the world's 2,000th Ramsar site. This is international recognition for the typical wetland ecosystem of the Dong Thap Muoi region.
